headline: Contract amendment for Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations Chad Mazza, 617 Transformer Project, and dual language school model at 617 Lexington Street.
summary: The meeting covers closed-door talks on union contracts and two lawsuits. Open business includes a contract amendment for Chad Mazza, the 617 Transformer Project, and budget transfer requests.

plain_text:
WALTHAM SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
 Waltham, Massachusetts 
 JAMES J. CANNON LECTURE HALL  617 LEXINGTON STREET 
 DOCKET  OCTOBER 21, 2026 
 5:30 p.m.  EXECUTIVE SESSION 
 1.  To conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective bargaining with the WSSA and/or to conduct negotiations 
 with the WSSA 
 2.  To conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective bargaining with the WSAA and/or to conduct negotiations 
 with the WSAA 
 3.  To conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective bargaining with the Waltham School MIS Technicians and/or 
 to conduct negotiations with the Waltham School MIS Technicians 
 4.  To conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective bargaining with the Waltham School Department Food 
 Service Workers and/or to conduct negotiations with the Waltham School Department Food Service Workers 
 5.  To conduct strategy sessions in preparation for negotiations with nonunion personnel and/or to conduct 
 negotiations with nonunion personnel  – Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations 
 6.  To conduct strategy sessions with respect to collective bargaining with the Waltham Building Maintenance Workers 
 Association and/or to conduct negotiations with the Waltham Building Maintenance Workers Association 
 7.  In accordance with Mass. G.L. c. 30A, Section 21(a)(3), to discuss strategy with respect to litigation if an open 
 meeting may have a detrimental effect on the litigating position of the public body and the chair so declares - 
 Waltham School Secretaries Association and the Waltham Public Schools MUP-26-12223 
 8.  In accordance with Mass. G.L. c. 30A, Section 21(a)(3), to discuss strategy with respect to litigation if an open 
 meeting may have a detrimental effect on the litigating position of the public body and the chair so declares - 
 Waltham School Secretaries Association and the Waltham School Committee MUP-26-12365 
 7:00 p.m.  REGULAR  MEETING 
 1.  PUBLIC INPUT 
 2.  STUDENT COUNCIL / STUDENT INPUT 
 3.  SCHOOL COUNCIL / PTO / SEPAC / BELPAC INPUT 
 4.  CONSENT AGENDA 
 a)  Minutes from the Regular Meeting held on October 7, 2026 
 b)  Retirements 
 c)  Resignations 
 d)  Donation from Watertown Savings Bank to the WHS Golf Team 
 e)  Donation from Watertown Savings Bank to the WHS Soccer Team 
 5.  COMMUNICATIONS 
 a)  Staff out of district request for the 2026-2027 school year 
 6.  SUPERINTENDENT’S UPDATE 
 a)  Miscellaneous Personnel 
 b)  Information 
 7.  CURRICULUM AND INSTRUCTION 
 a)  School Improvement Plan - MacArthur Elementary School 
 b)  School Improvement Plan - Stanley Elementary School 
 c)  School Improvement Plan - Waltham High School 
 8.  UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
 a)  Anti-Racism, Diversity, Equity and Inclusion 
 b)  Dual Language School Model and the Reutilization of 617 Lexington Street 
 c)  Waltham High School’s Career and Technical Education (CTE) Department 
 d)  Waltham High School Schedule 
 e)  Enrollment, Space and Data in the Waltham Public Schools 
 f)  School Committee Subcommittee Meetings 
 9.  NEW BUSINESS 
 a)  Waltham Public Schools District Policy and Training 
 b)  Proposed New Positions 
 c)  To vote to execute an Amendment to the Contract of Employment between the Waltham Public Schools 
 and Chad Mazza for the position of Assistant Superintendent for Finance and Operations 
 10.  FISCAL MATTERS 
 a)  FY ‘26 School Department End of Year Report 
 b)  617 Transformer Project 
 c)  FY ‘27 Budget Transfer Requests 
 d)  Bills on Warrant 
 11.  AGENDA ITEMS FOR FUTURE MEETINGS 
 The listings of matters are those reasonably anticipated by the Chair which may be discussed at the meeting. Not all items listed may in fact be 
 discussed and other items not listed may also be brought up for discussion to the extent permitted by law.
